#5243. Enjin Matrixchain Votes on OpenGov Today: What Changes for ENJ Holders on November 16

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Enjin holders vote through November 13 on moving Matrixchain to OpenGov on November 16. Here is how the nine tracks, the 1,000 ENJ deposit and conviction voting work, and what the Relaychain vote shows.

Enjin's new proposal deposit sounds steep at 1,000 ENJ. It's actually the cheap part.

Enjin holders have until today, November 13, to vote on moving the Matrixchain to the Fort Canning release. The referendum opened November 10. If it passes, the upgrade is targeted for November 16 at block #12,319,600, with the network moving from runtime 1.3.1 to 1.4.3. Enjin's Fort Canning announcement lays out the plan, and the official changelog carries the technical detail.

The Relaychain has already made the jump. Referendum #16 approved its upgrade on October 28, and it went live on November 9. The Matrixchain vote is the second half of one upgrade, and it is the half that changes how Matrixchain makes decisions from then on.

Early coverage reported the schedule and the headline numbers: nine tracks, 1,000 ENJ. The changelog and the governance portal show the mechanics behind them, and those mechanics change more than the headlines suggest.

Today, the Matrixchain runs its governance through the older Democracy, Council and Technical Committee pallets, the modules that handle proposals and votes. Fort Canning replaces all three with a new set: Referenda, Conviction Voting, Origins, Whitelist and the Enjin Fellowship. Under OpenGov, any account can submit a referendum on one of nine tracks, and from the moment the upgrade lands, Matrixchain's own upgrades go through that process.

A track is a lane for a particular kind of decision. Enjin's changelog describes the families: Root and the admin tracks for the highest-stakes changes, Whitelisted Caller for proposals the Fellowship fast-tracks, and two special tracks, Referendum Killer and Referendum Canceller, for stopping a proposal that shouldn't proceed. Matrixchain gets no treasury tracks: those, sized by how much a proposal would spend, stay on the Relaychain, where treasury requests now go. Each track has its own deposit, approval curve and enactment period, and the Enjin Fellowship can fast-track time-sensitive proposals.

Splitting decisions this way means a small treasury request doesn't face the same bar as a change to the chain's core. Riskier tracks demand larger deposits and more support, while smaller ones move faster and cost less.

The submission deposit rises from 0.025 ENJ to 1,000 ENJ on every track, a 40,000-fold increase. The deposit is refunded when a referendum passes or is canceled, and it exists to deter spam. As an illustration, using the roughly $66 million market cap reported in early October, ENJ traded near three cents, which would put 1,000 ENJ around $33.

That is only the entry ticket. The cost that matters comes next. A referendum also needs a decision deposit before it moves into voting, and the changelog lists steep figures: 2,500,000 ENJ on Root and Fellowship Admin, 1,000,000 ENJ on the other admin tracks, and 2,500 to 250,000 ENJ on the Relaychain's treasury tracks. At the same illustrative price, the 2.5 million ENJ Root deposit comes to roughly $80,000, about 0.12% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance.

So proposing is cheap, and pushing a proposal through is not. Anyone can raise an idea, but anyone who wants the network to vote on something big needs real stake in the outcome. The changelog says the same values apply on both chains, and Matrixchain adopts them for its new tracks.

The best evidence of how these votes work comes from the Relaychain referendum that has already finished. Enjin's governance portal shows referendum #16 as finalised, approved on October 28 and enacted on November 9.

The final tally on the page is small. Eleven voters cast 381,303.02 ENJ of conviction-weighted voting power, and all of it went to Aye: 100% in favor, 0 ENJ against. The page also shows raw, unweighted support of 271,303.2 ENJ, which it describes as the total balance backing the proposal and the figure the support curve uses. The conviction multiplier on the page runs from under 1x up to 6x.

Two numbers stand out. First, an entire chain upgrade passed with 271,303 ENJ of raw support, about 0.013% of the 2.02 billion ENJ total issuance, a figure worked out from the portal's number. Second, conviction added about 110,000 ENJ of weight on top of the raw balance, an average multiplier of roughly 1.4x. Voters picked up some extra weight, but most didn't lock their tokens for the long periods that earn the top multipliers.

A 100% Aye result says little by itself. A scheduled upgrade with no organized opposition passes easily, and the tally shows how thin engagement was.

Fort Canning adds the safeguard that thin turnout calls for. A referendum now needs a minimum share of total ENJ voting in support. The changelog sets 0.5% on Root and the admin tracks, 0.005% to 0.125% on the Relaychain's treasury tracks, 0.1% for Referendum Killer and 0.05% for Referendum Canceller. Measured against 2.02 billion ENJ, that means about 10.1 million ENJ on Root, roughly 101,000 to 2.5 million on the treasury tracks, about 2.02 million to kill a referendum and about 1.01 million to cancel one.

Referendum #16's 271,303 ENJ of raw support would clear the lowest treasury floor of about 101,000 ENJ, but it would miss the Root floor by a factor of about 37. The page doesn't show which track the referendum used, and a runtime upgrade typically sits on a high-stakes track, so the Root comparison works as an illustration and not as a finding. The floors also didn't exist when #16 passed, since Fort Canning introduced them.

That is the real change. Under the new rules, 11 wallets can't carry a chain-level decision on their own. Low turnout means failure, and proposals that matter will need far more ENJ behind them. Enjin's changelog says Matrixchain upgrades go through OpenGov starting with this one, which suggests today's vote still runs on the current system, so the floors will first bite on the first OpenGov referendum.

Holders who haven't voted can still do so through Enjin's governance portal before the window closes. Voting locks tokens, so the lock length is worth checking first. Enjin's support article on voting explains the trade-off: the longer the lock, the more a vote counts, and tokens stay locked until the period ends.

Node operators on the Matrixchain can wait for the result before upgrading, as Enjin has indicated, and then follow the changelog for the version to install. Relaychain operators already needed client version 1.8.1.

This vote is more about control than speed. OpenGov spreads decisions across tracks with deposits and support floors built for the weight of each choice, and it moves ENJ holders from voting on a handful of items to a standing governance system. The Relaychain's first vote showed how little participation it took under the old rules, and the first referenda after November 16 will show whether holders turn out for the new ones. If most proposals stall at the decision deposit, the system costs too much. If they clear with a handful of voters, the floors aren't doing their job. Either result will tell holders what their ENJ can do.

#5242. Strategy Sends Crucial Message on Bitcoin's Quantum Security

Strategy, the world's largest corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, has sent an important message regarding Bitcoin’s future resistance to quantum computing attacks.

The company, which was co-founded by renowned Bitcoin champion Michael Saylor, recently posted on X that the Bitcoin network can implement new security measures as and when they are needed.

“Quantum-resistant upgrades can be adopted if & when it's needed,” wrote Strategy.

These comments come at a time when the crypto industry is debating whether the rise of quantum computing could, in the long run, threaten Bitcoin’s cryptographic security.

Given that Bitcoin leverages elliptic curve cryptography for transaction security, quantum computing could pose a significant threat to Bitcoin.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer has the potential to reverse-engineer private keys from exposed public keys. This could give attackers access to the Bitcoin holdings associated with those keys.

At this point, there is no known publicly available quantum computer that can successfully break Bitcoin’s cryptography in this manner.

While speaking at the World Bank in Washington in October, Saylor said that the Bitcoin network would be able to defend itself against any realistic quantum computing threat by coming together and upgrading the software.

Saylor estimated that such an upgrade would take about 90 days once a worldwide consensus is reached on the need for quantum-resistant cryptography.

Saylor also warned against the hasty introduction of new cryptography. He reasoned that more complex security measures may themselves introduce weaknesses.

However, the 90-day estimate has come under scrutiny because such a network-wide shift would involve developers agreeing on technical changes and Bitcoin users moving their funds to new, secure addresses.

Interestingly, Strategy has also initiated efforts aimed at research and development for Bitcoin’s long-term security.

In July, Strategy was part of a group of seven major financial institutions and crypto companies, including BlackRock and Coinbase, that formed the Bitcoin Security Consortium.

The Bitcoin Security Consortium has committed $15 million over three years. One of the areas of focus of the consortium is post-quantum cryptography.

In fact, Bitcoin developers are already working on ways to address the quantum computing issue.

One of the most prominent proposals is Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360 (BIP-360). This BIP introduces a new type of transaction output, Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR).

Neither company is backing away. In fact, both are positioning themselves for a recovery that could dramatically revalue their massive crypto treasuries. The question is which strategy has the better chance of delivering the biggest payoff.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy acquired 485 BTC for $33.4 million between November 9 and November 15, according to its latest SEC filing. The company paid an average of $68,887 per coin, bringing its total holdings to 850,849 BTC.

That is a substantial paper loss, but Saylor’s accumulation strategy has never depended on buying every Bitcoin at the bottom. Strategy continues using capital markets to expand its position, betting that Bitcoin’s long-term appreciation will eventually overwhelm short-term volatility.

Its latest filing also revealed $244.7 million in proceeds from common stock sales. Strategy allocated $33.4 million toward Bitcoin purchases, while spending $228.1 million repurchasing its STRC preferred shares.

Tom Lee is playing a different game. BitMine’s Ethereum holdings reached 6,070,092 ETH following its latest disclosed purchase of 9,587 ETH. The position represents 4.97% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, bringing the company within touching distance of its ambitious 5% accumulation target.

🧵1/BitMine provided its latest holdings update for November 16, 2026$11.8 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":– 6,077,745 ETH at $1,823 per ETH (per @coinbase)– 216 Bitcoin (BTC)– $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast– $67 million stake in Eightco Holdings…

At recent prices around $1,820, those holdings are worth $11 billion. But BitMine has another advantage that Strategy cannot replicate with its Bitcoin treasury: staking income.

The company has already staked 5.23 million ETH, or more than 86% of its holdings. Tom Lee projected that fully staking its Ethereum treasury could generate approximately $359 million in annualized rewards.

That creates a potentially powerful combination. BitMine is accumulating a substantial share of Ethereum’s supply while putting most of its holdings to work.

Lee’s thesis extends beyond ETH price appreciation. He sees Ethereum benefiting from institutional tokenization, financial infrastructure moving onchain, and growing demand for blockchain-based settlement.

If those trends accelerate, BitMine could benefit from both Ethereum appreciation and recurring staking rewards.

This is where the competition gets interesting. Strategy has the larger dollar-denominated crypto treasury, but BitMine has a compelling argument for capital efficiency. Bitcoin offers a straightforward scarcity thesis, while Ethereum adds staking and exposure to expanding blockchain activity.

Strategy’s biggest advantage is its enormous Bitcoin position. With 850,849 BTC, even a substantial recovery in Bitcoin could translate into billions of dollars in additional treasury value.

BitMine, however, has built an Ethereum position approaching 5% of circulating supply. Its staking operation gives the company another potential source of returns while waiting for the next market expansion.

There is also a difference in what investors are buying. Strategy offers a concentrated Bitcoin treasury vehicle, while BitMine offers a leveraged corporate bet on Ethereum’s future financial infrastructure.

Our verdict? BitMine has the more productive treasury model, but Strategy remains the heavyweight in corporate crypto accumulation.

If Bitcoin leads the next recovery, Saylor could quickly reclaim the spotlight. If Ethereum outperforms and institutional adoption accelerates, Lee’s strategy could look considerably smarter.

Both companies are effectively making the same bet: today’s market weakness will look insignificant when the next major crypto cycle arrives.

The winner may ultimately depend on which asset leads that recovery. But neither Saylor nor Lee appears interested in waiting for confirmation before accumulating.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) is set to get more exposure in the U.S.-regulated financial market after the North American Derivatives Exchange (Nadex) self-certified a new strike event contract tied to the meme cryptocurrency's price.

On November 10, 2026, an official Nadex notice said the exchange certified a swap based on the price of SHIB at a specific time and date. The product, called the Shiba Inu Strike Event Contract, began trading on or after Nov. 13, 2026.

The filing is available through the official records of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The regulator’s database shows that the SHIB Strike Event Contract is certified as a swap, with November 10 listed as the certification date.

The product allows traders to wager that a particular price of SHIB will be attained or surpassed at some point in the future. This opens another avenue for market players to take positions based on the price fluctuations of Shiba Inu without having to buy or hold the underlying token.

Nadex (North American Derivatives Exchange) is a CFTC-regulated U.S. financial exchange acquired by Foris DAX Markets (part of Crypto.com), bringing the Shiba Inu product to a regulated platform.

Shiba Inu Japan community member Kuro reacted to the development, saying SHIB is now the underlying asset for a new financial product in the U.S.-regulated market.

"Nadex, an exchange owned by Crypto.com, has officially filed a new trading product based on SHIB’s price, and it has also been listed in the official records of the U.S. CFTC. This product lets traders predict whether SHIB will exceed a certain price at a specified time, alongside assets such as BTC, ETH, and XRP," Kuro added, saying another opportunity for SHIB to be used in the U.S. financial market has just opened up.

At the time of writing, SHIB was down 3.33% over the last 24 hours to $0.00000414 amid broader crypto market weakness that coincided with strength in the U.S. dollar.

The dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025 on Friday, following hotter-than-expected inflation earlier this week that increased expectations of further Fed tightening, pushing Treasury yields and the dollar higher while pulling down both cryptocurrencies and gold.

#5231. Hoskinson Credits Cardano’s Staking Model After Binance Hack Leaves Network Unaffected

Charles Hoskinson has credited the underlying architecture for keeping Cardano (ADA) and Midnight (NIGHT) unaffected by the recent Binance hack, arguing that years of deliberate design decisions are now paying off.

The Cardano founder acknowledged that the network’s early focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, liquid non-custodial staking, and the need for Layer-2 (L2) solutions built around its Extended UTXO (EUTXO) model, came in handy during the hacking incident.

Hoskinson went further, saying these were not accidental advantages but deliberate choices based on anticipating the blockchain industry’s evolving needs. Furthermore, he suggested that the recent hacking demonstrated the importance of building networks with security and resilience at their core.

Cardano’s staking model continues to grow, with the Cardano Foundation reporting that 57.6% of ADA’s circulating supply is staked.

Notably, every delegated coin backs a stake pool that helps produce blocks and secure the network.

Unlike traditional staking models that lock up assets, Cardano’s liquid staking allows holders to delegate their ADA while retaining full control. As a result, they can spend, transfer, or move their funds without first having to unstake them.

Therefore, this approach is unique because it combines network participation with financial flexibility while supporting a decentralized pool ecosystem. Additionally, it reduces reliance on centralized custodians, boosting the network’s broader resilience.

Meanwhile, Cardano is expanding its real-world utility since police in Uttar Pradesh, India’s most populous state, recently began using its blockchain technology to track forensic evidence in active criminal investigations.

More importantly, the Cardano Foundation said evidence scans and laboratory results will be recorded on-chain, creating a tamper-resistant audit trail designed to strengthen the integrity of investigations.

#5230. Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has doubled down on his comments about completing the blockchain's development. In an AMA, the Cardano founder was asked about finishing Cardano; he answered in the affirmative, saying yes, the roadmap was done.

In a recent livestream titled "Finishing Cardano," Hoskinson maintains that his job with Cardano was done. "My job is done with Cardano," he said, doubling down on his recent statements and on where things stand with Cardano.

Finishing Cardano https://t.co/LtFVLOHrxk

Hoskinson said he saw a barrage of criticism and negative comments after his remarks, with some speculating that he had failed, that Cardano was a failed project, or that he was leaving Cardano. He, however, maintains that there is no ambiguity in his statements.

Hoskinson revisited the launch of Cardano (ADA) in 2015 in response to critics who claimed that he or the Cardano project had failed.

"So, let's look at 2015. There was a crowd sale conducted to sell ADA into Japan. The price for this was less than 0.2 cents per ADA. And Bitcoin was actually used as the settlement system for this. They bought in yen and settled in Bitcoin. So there are even on-chain records of the sales tranche. The total amount of money raised was $72 million."

Highlighting the growth of the Cardano cryptocurrency, Hoskinson noted that the market valuation has increased immensely from an initial $72 million. "We built a network that went from a $72 million valuation to an all-time high of $100 billion," Hoskinson stated.

Cardano reached an all-time high price of $3.09 on September 2, 2021, which corresponded to an all-time-high market capitalization of nearly $100 billion at that peak.

Following ADA's drop from this ATH, Cardano's market valuation sits at $6.03 billion. Hoskinson maintains that this is still growth, up from an initial $72 million. "Even in its deflated state, everybody's saying it's destroyed and it's a dead coin and all these other things. It's $6 billion. It went from 72 to six," Hoskinson said.

Hoskinson specifically reiterated that the Cardano roadmap is not being abandoned and went on to reveal further growth credentials: "We delivered a fully decentralized, recursively self-improving ecosystem. We left behind a community-led and community-owned treasury that, at its all-time high, had $4 billion in value, and initiated a constitution."

"We built an entire on-chain governance system, wrote a constitution, got the entire community involved, and created a recursively self-improving system that's fully decentralized—the most decentralized cryptocurrency on the planet," Hoskinson added.

#5227. Binance Tightens Security With Zero-Knowledge Proof Upgrade

Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has continued to deploy new measures to strengthen security on its exchange after it suffered the biggest cyberattack ever seen in the history of crypto late last month.

In a bid to foster transparency and regain its users' trust, Binance has just announced the completion of a major upgrade to further strengthen its security.

In an announcement shared on November 14, Binance said that it has generated a new zero-knowledge proof for its Proof of Reserves (PoR) system.

According to Binance, the upgrade allows users to independently verify that it holds sufficient assets to cover their account balances on a 1:1 basis.

The exchange further shared snapshots to prove that it maintains reserves above its users' net account balances across six major cryptocurrencies, boosting their confidence in its operating standards.

It also added that the update covers all assets affected by the recent attack, and the exchange showcased its reserves for the following crypto assets: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether, BNB, Solana, and USDC.

While withdrawals are being restored in batches, with the last phase scheduled for next week, Binance has continued to improve its operations to replenish all affected assets and tighten security to regain users' trust.

Following its latest move, Binance revealed that its Bitcoin reserves are currently at 100.05%, slightly above the 100% mark. This means that Binance's Bitcoin reserves amount to about 688,283 BTC, substantially above its net user balances of 687,912 BTC.

The case is similar for the rest of the tokens: Ethereum reserves are at 100.02%, while BNB and USDC recorded ratios of 100.39% and 100.07%, respectively.

While Binance also reported stronger reserve ratios for USDT and SOL, at about 104.34% and 105.86%, respectively, it is evident that Binance holds more of these assets than the total amount owed to users.

Binance has specified that the Proof of Reserves covers assets that are in its custody on behalf of users, rather than its entire corporate holdings, assuring users that their funds are fully backed.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

Data from XRPL explorer Bithomp reveals that the Batch and Ticket features on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) are increasingly being adopted, with both setting new daily records in November.

The data indicates an increasing use of two XRPL features intended to enhance transaction flexibility and efficiency on the network.

Batch activity reached a new daily high for the month at 1.962 million on November 3, 2026. Ticket activity came next at 1.553 million on November 7, 2026, also setting a new November record. The increase indicates that these features are being embraced in the XRPL ecosystem. Batch functionality allows multiple transactions to be grouped and executed together and was activated on the XRPL mainnet on October 9, 2026.

The growth in batch activity, which neared 2 million on November 3, 2026, comes less than one month after its launch.

This is significant, as Batch is a prerequisite or accelerant for several high-value XRPL use cases already under contract or in the active pipeline, including atomic multi-party settlements. Institutional workflows (custody transfers, DvP settlement, cross-border payment finalization) require two or more accounts to act simultaneously.

On the other hand, tickets provide a way to reserve transaction sequence numbers, giving users more flexibility in managing transactions.

XRP Ledger metrics are in the green, with the transaction count up 75.9% to 4.3 million; active accounts jumped 128%, while XRP burned as fees rose 136%. Payments volume surged 137% in the last 24 hours to $1 billion, according to XRPScan data, while NFT mints rose 240% in the same timeframe.

Not only is the XRP Ledger seeing increased activity, but Ripple led stablecoin market cap growth by issuer over the past 24 hours, up $90.9 million, 4x the next issuer, multipli.fi, at $21.3 million.

Ripple's RLUSD market cap has grown 96% this year, across Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, to $2.7 billion from $1.4 billion in January. Most of that growth came in July, when Ripple launched Ripple Mint. RLUSD market cap stood just under $1.5 billion that month and rose to $2.3 billion by August.

In a milestone for the network, one year ago today, the first US ETF to hold only XRP began trading. Since then, US spot XRP ETFs have accumulated over 1.16 billion XRP.

#5217. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

Bitcoin is trading near $69,200 after another sharp daily decline. The chart shows that BTC has broken below the $75,000–$76,000 support zone, which now represents an important resistance area. The immediate level to watch is around $69,000.

A sustained break below it could expose the $64,000–$65,000 support area, followed by $60,000. On the upside, Bitcoin would need to reclaim $75,000 to signal a potential recovery and improve its short-term outlook.

Bitcoin faces several challenges heading into the next difficulty adjustment. The increase in miner-to-exchange transfers, combined with negative demand indicators, suggests that the market is struggling to attract sufficient buying interest.

Still, the Antpool transfers should not be interpreted as proof of widespread miner capitulation. The data identifies a large movement from one mining pool, but does not establish that the coins were sold.

The upcoming difficulty reduction could improve mining conditions and help struggling operators manage their costs. However, it is unlikely to resolve the broader weakness in Bitcoin demand.

Investors will be watching whether exchange transfers translate into actual selling and whether spot-market buyers return. A recovery in demand would help absorb additional supply and provide a stronger foundation for Bitcoin’s next move.

#5213. Bitcoin May Never See a New ATH Again, Peter Brandt Floats Grim Scenario as Bearish Pattern Emerges

Bitcoin investors may have witnessed the cryptocurrency’s final record-breaking rally, at least according to veteran trader Peter Brandt. The legendary chartist has sounded the alarm over a potentially massive bearish pattern emerging on Bitcoin’s weekly chart, warning that if the formation holds, the apex crypto’s October 2025 all-time high above $126,000 may never be surpassed in his lifetime. His alarming assessment comes as BTC reels from a brutal market downturn, adding fresh uncertainty to an already battered crypto market.

Peter Brandt has raised the possibility that Bitcoin may have already reached its ultimate price peak after spotting a potentially significant bearish formation on its weekly chart. In a November 15 post on X, the renowned chartist questioned whether BTC was developing a legitimate head-and-shoulders (H&S) top, a technical pattern often associated with a major trend reversal.

Brandt suggested that if the formation proves valid, he could construct a technical case that Bitcoin’s previous record high was its last, potentially remaining unbeaten for the rest of his lifetime. His warning is particularly striking given that Bitcoin reached a record of $126,080 in October 2025 before suffering a sharp correction.

The H&S formation typically features three peaks, with the middle one (the head) rising above the two surrounding peaks (the shoulders). The pattern is considered bearish when the price breaks below the neckline, which connects the two troughs separating these peaks. Such a breakdown could signal weakening buying pressure and open the door to further losses. In Bitcoin’s case, the asset is approaching a crucial support zone between $60,000 and $65,000, which could serve as the neckline of the potential bearish formation.

However, Brandt has not confirmed that Bitcoin has completed this formation. His assessment remains conditional on whether the chart structure represents a legitimate bearish reversal, meaning traders will likely watch the potential neckline for signs of confirmation.

Bitcoin has extended its recent decline, with selling pressure intensifying on Nov. 13 as the flagship cryptocurrency dropped below the psychologically significant $70,000 threshold for the first time since August. The latest downturn has deepened its weekly losses to approximately 14.8%, highlighting the growing bearish sentiment weighing on the broader crypto market.

Meanwhile, crypto analyst James Check has pointed to another worrying development, suggesting Bitcoin is experiencing its fourth capitulation event since reaching its all-time high. According to Check, daily realized losses have surged, doubling from about $420 million to more than $850 million in just 24 hours.

Check also offered a more optimistic perspective, arguing that Bitcoin has entered what he describes as a “deep value” zone. He noted that the cryptocurrency last traded in similar territory in February and late June this year, with the previous comparable occurrence dating back to the 2022 crypto bear market.

However, the pundit cautioned that entering this zone does not necessarily mean Bitcoin has reached its market bottom. Instead, he suggested that investors who begin gradually accumulating BTC at these levels could eventually benefit if historical patterns repeat, potentially turning the current market weakness into a long-term buying opportunity.

Bitwise’s Hunter Horsley has shared a glimpse into what might define the cryptocurrency market in 2027.

In a post on X, Horsley reflected on the institutional shift that happened in 2026, writing, "The story of 2026 will have been that the financial institutions all joined team crypto." Horsley also mentioned a recent X post by Charles Schwab, which said that crypto is playing an increasing role in many Americans’ investment journeys, citing the 2026 Modern Wealth Survey.

Charles Schwab everyone The story of 2026 will have been that the financial institutions all joined team crypto. 2027…

The Modern Wealth Survey is an online study conducted for Charles Schwab by Logica Research among a national sample of Americans from August 24 to September 17, 2026.

Charles Schwab’s survey results show that cryptocurrency investors are planning to invest more in the coming months, which will boost adoption. More than half of all respondents (60%) expect to add to their holdings in the next 12 months, compared with ETF owners (56%) and stock owners (52%).

The interest of the participants is driven by the long-term potential. Growth potential and portfolio diversification are the most commonly cited benefits by owners and those interested in crypto. According to the survey, more than half of Americans familiar with cryptocurrency say it is important or essential to building wealth.

Half of those who own cryptocurrency see it as a complement to traditional investments, while more than two in five Americans familiar with cryptocurrency expect it to become a more popular investment; Millennials are the most likely generation to own and be interested in cryptocurrency.

The survey also found that Americans familiar with cryptocurrency are considering a range of ways to participate.

According to a recent Binance research report, institutional appetite for digital assets appears to be well established. In the EY-Parthenon and Coinbase 2026 survey, 73% of institutions intend to increase their digital asset investments this year. AIMA and PwC find 55% of traditional hedge funds now hold crypto, up from 47% in 2024.

But that demand flows mostly into passive wrappers. Of those surveyed, 81% prefer spot exposure through a registered vehicle. This is seen as a reflection of market infrastructure rather than manager selection.

A large cluster of leveraged long positions around the $860 price level has traders on guard for a possible liquidation event that may result in increased volatility for Zcash (ZEC).

A liquidation cluster is an area where many leveraged positions could be liquidated if the price of the asset moves against the traders. CoinGlass data shows a long liquidation cluster worth $1.4 million is near $860.

Zcash is currently trading at $877, and a move lower to $860 could put long-position holders under liquidation pressure.

If ZEC approaches this level, forced liquidations could add to the selling pressure and possibly accelerate a move to the downside. Liquidations occur when traders who have borrowed or leveraged money are unable to maintain margin on their positions.

But the presence of a liquidation cluster does not mean that the price will fall to $860. It identifies a potential area of market vulnerability rather than a confirmed price target.

Zcash fell below the $1,000 mark amid a weeklong selloff further compounded by concerns over leadership turmoil at Nvidia Corp., which weighed on the artificial intelligence trade.

A broader weakness in the crypto market coincided with strength in the U.S. dollar. On Friday, the dollar index reached its highest level since April 2025, following hotter-than-expected inflation earlier this week that increased expectations of further Fed tightening, pushing Treasury yields and the dollar higher while pulling down both cryptocurrencies and gold.

Zcash fell to a low of $861 early in Saturday's session, after marking seven consecutive days of losses since November 7, 2026. If today ends in a loss, it will mark the eighth consecutive day of losses. Zcash lost momentum after dropping below the 50 DMA, a support level that had buoyed its price surge in August 2026, and a return above it is crucial for its price recovery.

Large buy walls are present, according to on-chain data, at $845, $811, and $805, marking key support levels for Zcash that might halt the bears' rampage.

Emerging in late 2024 from a high-profile merger between APX Finance and Astherus, the platform operates across major Layer-1 and Layer-2 blockchains, including BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Ethereum, and Solana. It is designed to bridge the user experience gap between centralized exchanges and on-chain trading

ASTER’s tokenomics could also become an important price driver. Since June 2026, 99% of daily platform fees have been used for ASTER buybacks, while an equal amount is burned from reserves. These burns are planned to continue until total supply falls toward 3 billion tokens.

That follows a rough six months, when MSTR had dropped -37.3%. Perplexity AI predicts where MSTR stock will go over the next few months, and it may surprise some given the current bearish landscape across crypto and tech stocks.

The latest headlines mostly focus on capital management. Q3 earnings landed on 29 October, and EPS of $44.75 beat the $21.50 consensus, though revenue of $125.4M missed. The profit is mainly a mark-to-market Bitcoin gain. Last week’s filing was more unusual.

The company sold about 2.05 million shares of MSTR, generating net proceeds of $283.8M. Of this amount, the company allocated only $81.9M to purchasing Bitcoin (BTC), while using $188.3M to repurchase its preferred stock (STRC).

The company currently holds 850,364 BTC, with an average acquisition cost of $75,456 per coin. Bitcoin is currently trading just above $64,000 after a tragic -14% weekly crash, now leaving Saylor underwater.

The short-term outlook for MSTR is weak. The stock is currently trading below all four major exponential moving averages (EMAs), with the daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) near 41, indicating soft momentum. Additionally, other metrics show a negative Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD).

The 200-day moving average, which is around $133, has provided support so far, but the stock is below its 20-day average ($139) and 50-day average ($149). The key levels to watch are as follows:

– If the stock fails to hold above $110, the next support level is at $102. – Over the past six months, support has been found near $87. – Resistance is located between $126 and $130, which is the first major hurdle where the moving averages converge. – Should the stock break above this resistance, the next level to watch is around $186.

The overall trend remains bearish until MSTR can reclaim the $136–140 range on a closing basis. If support at $110 fails, it could open the door to lower price levels.

The $4.77Bn reserve can cover preferred dividends, alleviating concerns about forced selling. Additionally, buying back its stock below par could enhance Bitcoin’s per-share value.

XRP's price correction of more than 43% from its October high of $1.55 has brought a critical long-term support trendline into focus.

A multi-year ascending triangle dating back to 2017 points to potential support near $0.78 and major resistance around $3.50.

A confirmed breakout above $3.50 could set up an ambitious long-term rally toward $18, although the pattern remains unconfirmed.

XRP price could be heading toward $0.78 as a nearly decade-long chart pattern approaches a crucial test. The token has already suffered a steep correction from its October peak of $1.55, bringing its rising weekly support trendline into focus. While the $3.50 resistance remains the key barrier for a major bullish breakout, XRP may need to endure another correction before that recovery becomes possible. Will the $0.78 level become XRP’s next major bottom?

XRP’s latest correction has put a critical support level back on the radar. A weekly chart analysis identifies a large ascending triangle that has been developing since 2017, with successive market lows forming a rising support trendline and resistance holding near $3.50.

XRP COULD BOTTOM AT $0.78A big ascending triangle appears to have been developing on XRP’s weekly chart since 2017.With $XRP now down more than 43% from its October high of $1.55, this structure suggests the correction could extend toward the triangle’s rising trendline at… pic.twitter.com/AjOOE5oKET

The structure suggests that buyers have consistently entered the market at higher levels during previous downturns. However, XRP has yet to secure a sustained breakout above the triangle’s upper boundary.

Now, after falling more than 43% from its October high of $1.55, XRP is moving closer to the pattern’s rising support. The analysis projects that trendline toward approximately $0.78, making it the next major level to watch if selling pressure continues.

A move toward $0.78 would represent another substantial decline from the October peak. More importantly, it would put the long-term bullish structure to its most important test in years.

The $3.50 level is more than another resistance zone. It represents the upper boundary of the multi-year ascending triangle and the price XRP would need to overcome to confirm a major bullish breakout.

A sustained weekly close above this barrier could change the broader technical outlook. However, traders would also want to see XRP revisit $3.50 and hold it as support. Such a retest would provide stronger evidence that buyers have taken control of the long-term trend.

Until then, the bullish breakout remains unconfirmed. XRP’s immediate challenge is to stop the decline and establish a stronger base before attempting another move toward its major resistance.

The $18 projection is the most ambitious part of the long-term chart setup. It represents a potential upside target if XRP completes the ascending triangle breakout and sustains its move above $3.50. The scenario would require several stages: buyers first defend the rising trendline, XRP rebuilds upward momentum, and the token eventually clears the horizontal resistance. A successful retest of $3.50 could then strengthen the case for a much larger advance.

However, the distance between the current correction and that potential target makes $18 a speculative long-term projection rather than a near-term forecast. Broader crypto market conditions and sustained demand would also determine whether such an expansion is achievable.

#5199. XRP Scams Soar Across Social Media, Here’s What To Watch Out For

Scam attempts aimed at XRP holders have reached intense levels, according to recent alerts from a well-known figure in the XRP Ledger community. Vet, a pseudonymous X account who also works as a dUNL validator while contributing to the XRP Ledger

Foundation has used his platform several times to highlight the growing threat.

In a recent check using platform data tools, he found that around 11.5 million posts directed at the XRP community appeared within a single 30-day stretch.

The vast majority dangled fake airdrops or reward schemes designed to trick people into handing over funds or linking their wallets. He described the sheer number as eye-opening and pushed users to stay highly alert.

Vet has also pointed out how quickly fraudsters react to genuine positive news. When real companies announce partnerships or integrations involving the XRP Ledger, scammers often rush to set up lookalike addresses and launch tokens that borrow those brand names.

His advice is straightforward: treat every unexpected offer with suspicion, and trust only details that come directly from the company’s official channels. In many cases, the real institutions never publish public issuer addresses.

He has spoken about the constant stream of scam tags that can make notifications almost impossible to manage. Seeing community members engage with these posts frustrates him, and he keeps returning to the same clear message. No one is giving away free XRP. The safest move is usually to ignore the approach completely.

Even specific token launches have drawn his scrutiny. After a large Japanese firm introduced a yen-backed stablecoin, Vet warned that any version appearing on the XRP Ledger under a similar ticker was almost certainly fake without an official issuer confirmation.

His ongoing posts underline a simple reality. Rising interest in XRP attracts more bad actors who try to cash in on the attention. For everyday holders, staying skeptical and double-checking everything remains the best protection.

#5194. DTCC to Bring Tokenized Stocks and Treasuries to Solana in 2027

DTCC to Bring Tokenized Stocks and Treasuries to Solana in 2027

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), the backbone of U.S. securities settlement, plans to bring its tokenized securities to Solana, it announced on Thursday.

The firm will connect the DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) to the Solana network, allowing eligible assets held by its Depository Trust Company (DTC) subsidiary to be converted into tokens on Solana. The integration is planned for the second half of 2027.

BREAKING: @The_DTCC to tokenize custodied assets on Solana. announced plans to connect the DTCC Tokenization Service to Solana, enabling the tokenization of eligible DTC-custodied assets on the network.

The integration is planned for the second half of 2027, further advancing… pic.twitter.com/gXszWFgUOX

"DTCC is bringing regulated, DTC-tokenized securities to another major blockchain ecosystem, giving market participants greater choice in where they access and utilize tokenized assets," DTCC CEO Frank La Salla said.

DTS went live on October 28 on the Canton Network and DTCC's own private blockchain, built on the Besu framework, with more networks due to be added in 2027, according to DTCC's launch announcement. The service creates tokenized "digital twins" of securities held at DTC, which custodies more than $114 trillion in assets. Solana joins Stellar and Circle's Arc blockchain, which are expected to be added in 2027, according to a DTCC fact sheet.

Under a no-action letter from the SEC, the service is limited to a defined set of highly liquid assets, including Russell 1000 stocks, ETFs tracking major indexes, and U.S. Treasuries. Morgan Stanley said last week it had tokenized U.S. stocks and Treasuries through the service.

Tokens issued on Solana "will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," said Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

Solana has been actively courting traditional finance in recent months, with Solana Foundation head of institutional Nick Ducoff arguing that, "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale." He added that institutions are "already issuing, settling and deploying capital" on the network, in a tweet shared by Solana's official account.

Last month, the Solana Foundation unveiled an open standard for institutional settlement developed with input from J.P. Morgan, and the network completed its Alpenglow upgrade, cutting the time it takes for transactions to become final to roughly 150 milliseconds.

Solana is also lining up more venues for tokenized stocks. Trading platform Formation has notified the SEC of plans to trade tokenized U.S. stocks on Solana, starting with Galaxy and Forward Industries.

We matched Polymarket’s odds of Huang’s return with a 24/7 Nvidia stock contract on Hyperliquid. Musk’s post lifted the odds but barely moved the stock. A sharper jump in the odds on Sunday evening did: the stock rose 3% within two hours, then gave it all back by Monday.

So how is Nvidia’s stock reacting, one day before earnings?

Musk posted on X that “a petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.” He had said earlier that hiring Huang would be “an honor.”

The petition is hosted at standwithjensen.com. Signers report their own job titles, and the site does not verify them. More than 7,500 say they work at the company, about 18% of its staff.

The company says it is choosing a search firm for the CEO role and has not formally approached any candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress runs the company in the meantime.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

Nasdaq is shut on weekends, but the stock still trades around the clock as a perpetual contract, a futures-style contract with no expiry date, on Hyperliquid. To see whether the Jensen Huang petition moved the stock, we lined up its hourly price with Polymarket’s odds that Huang rejoins by December 31, 2026.

Polymarket’s longer bets show how far the Jensen Huang petition still has to go. Traders give Huang a 37.5% chance of rejoining by the end of 2027, but only 5.6% by November 30.

EXPLORE: Elon Musk’s Grok AI Predicts an Explosive Move for Solana Crypto

On the daily chart, Hyperliquid’s NVDA contract trades at $156.93. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $199.26, and its 200-day EMA at $206.42. On Nasdaq, the shares closed Friday at $162.85, down 18.6% since November 4.

The Jensen Huang petition has moved the odds more than the stock. Musk’s backing barely shifted the price, and Sunday’s jump faded within a day. Tuesday’s earnings, the first under Kress, are likely to matter more to Nvidia shares than any petition.

#5191. New Monero Privacy Update Might Be Coming Soon: Key Improvement

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.

PR 11743 was opened on November 13 and is currently pending review. It is an updated version of a PR opened on November 8 by contributor vtnerd. After receiving feedback from another Monero developer, vtnerd, the PR was updated.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P and then passes it to the regular Monero network.

Currently, when a Monero node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P, it relays that transaction to the rest of the Monero network.

While the transaction is technically private as it travels into the node, once it reaches Monero's public peers, the transaction is no longer private. This PR proposes that Monero nodes will only accept transactions from Tor and I2P peers over incoming connections. Transactions received over outgoing Tor and I2P connections would be ignored.

Once accepted, the transaction would be subject to a random delay before being relayed to the rest of the Monero network using Monero's existing transaction relay protocol, Dandelion++. Currently, a user can instruct their node to broadcast their transaction immediately.

Over Tor and I2P connections, this request would be ignored. No transaction would be exempt from the random delay.Being able to link a transaction's timing between the anonymity network and the Monero network is an easy way to deanonymize a user. If a transaction is broadcast to the Monero network immediately after being received from Tor, an observer watching both networks can link the two.

This is a similar concept to a previous PR from vtnerd that would have introduced a randomized delay when relaying transactions from Tor and I2P to the Monero network.

While the amount of code that would need to be modified is not particularly large, this does close a hole for users that rely on Tor and I2P to obscure their location.

When the patch lands in a release is yet to be confirmed. The PR is also labeled for a backport, so it might reach the current release branch as well.

#5190. 7 Liquid Staking Platforms and Blockchains to Know in 2026

Liquid staking has become a big part of decentralized finance (DeFi). It lets crypto holders earn staking rewards without locking their assets away completely. And as more blockchains look for ways to put capital to better use, liquid staking is spreading beyond Ethereum into ecosystems like Solana and Casper Network.

With traditional staking, you commit your tokens to help secure a proof-of-stake blockchain, and in return you usually canât do much else with them until you unstake. Liquid staking takes a different route. You get a token that represents your staked assets, and these liquid staking tokens (LSTs) can often be traded, moved, or used in supported DeFi apps while the original tokens keep earning staking rewards in the background.

Todayâs market includes decentralized protocols, exchange-run services, and solutions built for specific blockchains. Here are seven liquid staking platforms and ecosystems worth knowing in 2026.

Lido is one of the longest-running liquid staking protocols on Ethereum. It lets users stake ETH without running their own validator or meeting Ethereumâs 32 ETH minimum for a solo validator. Stake ETH through Lido and you receive stETH, a token that represents your position.

Unlike traditional staking, where your assets sit idle, stETH can be put to work across supported DeFi platforms for things like lending and providing liquidity. Lido is now a core part of Ethereumâs staking setup and a clear example of how liquid staking links network security with wider DeFi activity. Its size has also fueled an ongoing debate about validator concentration and decentralization.

Casper Network is bringing liquid staking to its proof-of-stake ecosystem, giving CSPR holders a new way to help secure the network while keeping their funds liquid. With Casper 2.0, liquid staking is built directly into the networkâs core protocol rather than added on through a third party. Users stake CSPR and receive sCSPR, a token representing their staked position.

Casper has partnered with WiseLending, a lending and borrowing protocol built on the network, to extend what sCSPR can do. The underlying CSPR keeps securing the network and earning rewards, while sCSPR can be held, swapped, or used in supported apps across the Casper ecosystem.

This matters because networks increasingly want staking to do more than generate passive income. By tying staking to DeFi, Casper aims to give token holders more freedom in how they manage and use their assets. For younger DeFi ecosystems, liquid staking can also help new financial apps grow. It creates assets that represent staked capital, so users donât have to give up their staking positions to take part.

Rocket Pool offers another take on Ethereum liquid staking, with a strong focus on decentralizing who runs validators. Users stake ETH and receive rETH, a token that reflects the value of their staked ETH plus rewards earned. Rather than paying out rewards by adding more tokens to your balance, rETH is built to grow in value relative to ETH as rewards build up.

Rocket Pool also supports independent node operators, which spreads staking across a wider group of participants. For anyone who wants to stake ETH without managing a validator, itâs an alternative to the larger providers, with a liquid token included.

Jito has become one of the best-known liquid staking providers on Solana. It pairs regular staking rewards with extra rewards from maximal extractable value (MEV). Stake SOL through Jito and you receive JitoSOL, which represents your staked assets and the rewards they earn.

JitoSOL works across supported Solana DeFi apps, so you can use it for lending, providing liquidity, and more. Jito shows how liquid staking providers can stand out through the way they generate rewards. Its deep ties to Solana DeFi also show how an LST can become a useful asset in its own right, well beyond its original staking role.

Marinade Finance is another established liquid staking protocol on Solana. It lets users stake SOL while keeping flexibility through its mSOL token. Deposit SOL into Marinadeâs liquid staking product and you receive mSOL, which represents your staked position and reflects rewards earned over time.

You can use mSOL across supported Solana DeFi apps, including lending protocols and liquidity pools. Marinade puts a lot of weight on spreading stake across many validators, which supports network decentralization while still giving users access to staking rewards. Together with Jito, it shows how varied liquid staking on Solana has become, with users able to pick from different validator strategies, reward structures, and DeFi integrations.

Coinbase offers liquid staking through its Ethereum staking service and Coinbase Wrapped Staked ETH, better known as cbETH. Eligible users can stake ETH on Coinbase and wrap their staked position into cbETH. That lets them transfer the token or use it in supported apps without unstaking the underlying ETH first.

Unlike decentralized protocols such as Lido or Rocket Pool, Coinbase is a centralized service where a major crypto exchange manages the staking for you. That makes it a good example of how liquid staking has grown beyond DeFi protocols to include exchange-based options. Users should still weigh the custody setup, reliance on the platform, and eligibility rules that come with a centralized provider.

Binance offers Ethereum liquid staking through WBETH, or Wrapped Beacon ETH, a token that represents staked ETH and the rewards it earns. Like rETH, WBETH is designed to rise in value relative to ETH as rewards build up, rather than adding tokens to your balance. It can also be transferred or used in supported DeFi apps, depending on network and platform compatibility.

As with Coinbase, Binance shows how centralized exchanges now compete in liquid staking alongside independent DeFi protocols. It may suit users who already stake through exchanges, though custody, withdrawal terms, and platform risk are all worth thinking about.

All liquid staking platforms aim to free up staked capital, but how they do it can vary a lot. Some, like Lido and Rocket Pool, are decentralized protocols. Others, like Coinbase and Binance, are run by exchanges. And ecosystems such as Casper and Solana show how liquid staking can be built into different network designs and DeFi setups.

Key things to compare include validator decentralization, staking rewards, protocol fees, smart contract security, token liquidity, and how many DeFi apps support the token. Liquid staking also comes with risks that traditional staking doesnât carry in the same way. LSTs can trade below the value of the assets they represent, smart contracts can have bugs, and using LSTs in other DeFi activities can expose you to liquidation or liquidity risk. Staking rewards also vary and are never guaranteed.

Liquid staking is changing how people engage with proof-of-stake networks. Instead of choosing between staking and DeFi, users can now do both, helping secure a network while keeping more control over their assets. Lido and Rocket Pool helped build the Ethereum liquid staking market, while Jito and Marinade brought the model to Solana. Casper Networkâs partnership with WiseLending shows how other proof-of-stake ecosystems are adding liquid staking to their expanding DeFi infrastructure.

As blockchains keep building new financial tools, the ability to earn staking rewards without giving up liquidity may become an increasingly important feature of the crypto world.

#5187. NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

Home » Exchanges » NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

NYSE has selected Avalanche technology to support settlement for its planned tokenized securities platform, bringing round-the-clock stock trading and faster settlement closer to reality, pending regulatory approval.

The New York Stock Exchange is mixing together blockchain technology and traditional finance. It selected Avalanche to power the settlement infrastructure of its upcoming tokenized securities platform. The decision is part of a growing effort to bring crypto trading and its benefits to traditional finance.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the partnership will see Avalanche provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue. One of the goals is to enable round-the-clock trading, as well as clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, all of which still require regulatory changes.

NYSE has organized a yearlong test, and afterwards Avalanche emerged as a favorite provider and one that could meet its needs and provide a seamless inclusion of blockchain traders into the fold of the stock exchange account holders.

The platform is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks, meaning Avalanche will not necessarily host every tokenized stock traded through the venue. The technology will therefore mostly be used to record and settle transactions.

NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said that the focus was on speed, reliability, and predictable costs. Ava Labs CEO Emin Gün Sirer also highlighted the importance of dedicated infrastructure.

The crypto infrastructure industry is huge, and there’s a growing list of cryptocurrency exchanges, including those reviewed by CryptoManiaks, to choose from. Platforms made for transfers and smart contracts automating payments have also grown and now include thousands of providers. NYSE chose Avalanche due to some of its unique characteristics.

Avalanche’s architecture allows businesses to create dedicated blockchain networks with rules tailored to their operational and regulatory requirements. It creates a flexibility that traditional financial institutions are looking for.

Stock exchanges handle countless transactions, and stability is the most important feature they are looking for. Another important feature is atomic settlement. It allows the transfer of securities and corresponding payment to occur as part of the same transaction. Therefore, there’s no chance one side of a trade is completed while the other remains outstanding.

NYSE also plans to operate a custom blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than relying directly on Avalanche’s public network.

The decision reflects a broader effort to tokenize traditional markets and get the best of both worlds. That way, crypto companies won’t dominate the space, but can combine their features with those of the stock market.

Nasdaq is among the NYSE’s most prominent competitors. It, too, has developed tokenized stock infrastructure and is pursuing partnerships that could help distribute blockchain-based securities. This is done in cooperation with Kraken and in a way that NYSE is responding to the demands of a competitive market.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), a central institution in US securities settlements, also has plans to introduce tokenization. It plans to use blockchain to support securities custody and transfers.

NYSE has also expanded its list of partners. It now includes Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate. These developments show that financial institutions are fighting to establish the underlying infrastructure that will determine how digital securities are traded, transferred, and settled.

What Tokenized Stocks Could Mean for Investors

Tokenized stocks could change how investors are accessing traditional financial markets. The possibility of trading outside of business hours is the first thing investors have been looking for, alongside faster settlements. The NYSE’s broader platform plans include stablecoin-based funding, fractional share trading, and immediate settlement.

Ownership will also change. The NYSE has indicated that its platform will support tokenized shares that are fungible with traditionally issued securities, as well as securities originally issued in digital form. Shareholders will continue to have the same rights as traditional owners, meaning they’ll receive dividends and take part in corporate governance.

All of these benefits aren’t regulated, and before investors can take advantage of them, traditional regulatory bodies need to act and establish rules and guidelines for the new features.

Despite the institutional interest, the NYSE’s Avalanche-powered project still faces several challenges before it can become a functioning alternative to conventional securities infrastructure. The platform needs to demonstrate that it can maintain the safeguards expected of a major US stock exchange.

There’s also a distinction between Avalanche’s institutional adoption and the potential benefits for its native AVAX token. It’s not clear if the cooperation with NYSE will generate demand for AVAX. The project will depend on its ability to attract issuers, brokers, and investors while delivering reliable settlement.

#5186. SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi Brings Its Bank-Issued Stablecoin to Polygon’s Payments Stack

SoFi is widening the reach of its digital dollar, bringing SoFiUSD, the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank, onto Polygon’s payments infrastructure as banks and fintechs push stablecoins deeper into everyday money movement.

Polygon Labs said Thursday that SoFiUSD is now live on Polygon Open Money Stack, a payments layer that bundles fiat on- and off-ramps, embedded wallets and cross-chain settlement into a single integration.

The move adds Polygon alongside Ethereum and Solana, the networks SoFiUSD already runs on, and lets SoFi’s more than 17 million members buy, sell, hold, and convert the token on Polygon directly in the SoFi app, without opening a separate crypto wallet or manually bridging assets between chains.

“SoFi is well positioned to bring stablecoins into mainstream finance because it combines the regulatory foundation of a national bank with the reach of a major consumer and enterprise technology platform,” said Marc Boiron, CEO of Polygon Labs.

The expansion lands as stablecoins move beyond crypto trading into the plumbing used to settle card payments, pay businesses, and send money across borders.

On Polygon Open Money Stack, SoFiUSD joins USDC, USDT and PayPal’s PYUSD, and can connect to the wallets, banking rails, and local currencies businesses need for payouts, settlement and cross-border transfers, opening up uses well beyond consumer trading.

The token is redeemable one-to-one for U.S. dollars and issued by SoFi Bank, which is regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.

SoFi launched SoFiUSD late last year across Ethereum and Solana as the first stablecoin from a U.S. national bank, and it already settles the company’s entire card program over Mastercard’s network. The firm has been building out a broader digital-money suite, recently launching SoFi Earn, a tokenized deposit that pays 4.40% yield and converts one-to-one into SoFiUSD.

For Polygon, the addition deepens a payments business that has become one of the network’s calling cards.

Polygon recently extended Open Money Stack to Solana, and the chain has processed more than $3 trillion in lifetime stablecoin transfer volume, according to the company. Visa and Mastercard support stablecoin settlement on Polygon, while Stripe uses it to route USDC payments for merchants in more than 150 countries.

SoFiUSD is a payment stablecoin, not a bank deposit, and is not FDIC- or SIPC-insured, bank-guaranteed or legal tender.

#5185. Cardano's Hoskinson Says Everyone Will Be Happy Next Year

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is sending out a hopeful message to the crypto space in the wake of a brutal market crash that is causing ADA to come very close to falling out of the top 20 crypto assets.

Recently, Hoskinson took to X to respond to a frustrated Cardano fan who posted a screenshot showing ADA falling almost 10% in the last 24 hours.

“It’s all going to be ok,” said Hoskinson. “Everyone will be happy next year after all this madness, hate and idiocy.”

The recent crypto market crash has proven to be extremely brutal for a lot of different assets, and Cardano is certainly one of the worst affected.

In recent trading, ADA has fallen all the way down to around $0.15.

At these levels, ADA is currently down around 95% from its all-time high of $3.09, which was reached in September 2021, based on data from CoinGecko.

This represents an almost complete loss of investment value for those who bought at the all-time high.

Overall, Cardano is also down around 35% in the last month and almost 60% since the start of 2026.

As a result, Cardano’s market cap has fallen all the way down to around $5.7 billion, with ADA dropping to 18th place in CoinGecko’s crypto rankings.

This is a very precarious position for the once-dominant altcoin Cardano, which is now extremely close to falling out of the top 20.

It seems as though there are a few different factors at play behind Cardano’s poor performance.

First of all, there has been a huge sell-off in the broader crypto market. Bitcoin has seen major drops, leading to more selling pressure on major altcoins.

This decline has coincided with a falling technology stock market, ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty, outflows from crypto investment products, and mass liquidations of leveraged positions.

That said, there are clearly some issues with Cardano beyond the wider market struggles.

For one, Cardano has faced a lot of criticism over the years for the blockchain’s relatively low adoption, even after years of development. This is especially evident when compared to other chains like Ethereum and Solana.

In fact, Cardano’s decentralized finance ecosystem has recently seen around $46 million in total value locked, as reported by DefiLlama.

Celestia [TIA] has had a packed month so far. Their latest breakdown of how Voyager works also has people talking.

In the month gone by, Celestia launched Eden, an EVM chain for testing how AI agents trade.

Fibre went live on mainnet on 20th October, adding a lane for data uploads of around 128MB, up from 8MB. On the 29th, they launched Voyager, a payments layer for AI agents.
