#5182. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO, With CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief

Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia, ending a 33-year tenure at the helm of the chipmaker he co-founded, after reports of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a senior company executive.

Huang has stepped down as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately, Nvidia said on Thursday. Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer since 2013, will serve as interim CEO while remaining CFO, as the board searches for a permanent successor from both inside and outside the company. Nvidia did not give a reason for Huang's resignation, but thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

NVIDIA announces CEO transition. Read the release: https://t.co/MTTUvFHCJA

— NVIDIA Newsroom (@nvidianewsroom) November 12, 2026

The board also named Harvey Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of chip design software company Synopsys, as its first-ever chair.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Jones said.

Kress said she was "committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years." Nvidia will report its third-quarter results as scheduled on Tuesday, the company said.

Nvidia shares were down 7.7% at $160.28 shortly after the market opened on Thursday, having fallen as low as $148.80, according to Yahoo! Finance data.

Huang's departure comes four days after he acknowledged in a letter to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, prompting Nvidia's board to open an independent investigation. He had told the board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, The New York Times reported.

The Times had reported in October that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, while the Financial Times later reported that a U.S. government memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied the allegations.

On Wednesday, the Times reported that Huang had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal later reported that the board was preparing to oust him, adding to the pressure on the CEO.

The scandal has wiped hundreds of billions of dollars off Nvidia's market value, with the company losing about $430 billion in two days earlier this week. Nvidia and Huang also face a proposed shareholder class action, and lawmakers had threatened to subpoena him.

Huang ran Nvidia with about 60 executives reporting directly to him and has said he did not believe in succession planning, leaving the company without an obvious successor.

Prior to the announcement of Huang's resignation, one person inside the company had told the Financial Times that naming Kress as interim CEO would be the simplest option. Other potential candidates cited by the paper's sources include Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data center business, and Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive.

Huang remains Nvidia's largest shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6%, according to the Journal.

Bitcoin [BTC] closed in the red for the third consecutive day, with its price sliding to $67,000 on the charts. So far, the fall in prices has been driven by both whales and retail traders.

However, this pattern could be changing soon as Bitcoin’s sentiment starts to flip gradually. For instance, Hyperliquid whales turned back to the net long after two weeks of shorting BTC. This was the first selling period for them since March.

In fact, the daily mean of net long and net short grew from -1700 BTC on 8th November to around 900 BTC at press time. This seemed to imply that whales have been buying the dip below $70,000.

During the rally, which started in August, these whales went long. They subsequently sold the top. However, that does not guarantee that they will be right again.

On the other hand, retail traders have been showing signs of capitulation. In fact, BTC’s monthly change in Retail Investor Demand declined to around -10% after a sharp rise to over 17% as the price approached $80,000.

This fall in participation by retailers, volumes below $10K, have been common during BTC’s correction.

When looking at historical patterns, it is clearly evident that when retailers capitulate, the prices tend to reverse. Thus, going against the crowd may help investors catch a move, either to the downside or the upside early enough.

Still, that does not mean that the contrarian signal always works. Even though it may be an ideal time to build positions.

This action forced leveraged traders out as supported by the sharp decline in OI. So, if BTC price stabilizes while OI stays at these levels, it would mean a rebound will be driven more by spot demand than leverage.

Therefore, whale positioning and retail capitulation could be a signal for a sustainable BTC recovery.

However, it needs to be backed by capital inflows from the market in the form of ETFs and spot buying, among others.

Home » Trendsetter News » Wall Street Trading Booms on Crypto Exchanges. Which Tokens Benefit?

Crypto exchanges are seeing a surge in trading tied to traditional markets, but will token holders benefit most?

Crypto exchanges handled $3.16 trillion in trading tied to stocks, gold, oil and other traditional markets over the period tracked by research cited in a new Firehustle video episode.

The channel’s host, discussing crypto investment themes, argues that the important question is not how much trading these platforms attract, but whether that activity actually benefits HYPE, ONDO and INJ holders.

The figures, attributed to CoinMarketCap research covering 19 exchanges, describe trading exposure to traditional markets, not necessarily purchases of underlying shares. According to Fire Hustle, monthly volume climbed from roughly $100 billion in January to $800 billion in August, with stocks accounting for 62.3% of activity.

The expert identifies Hyperliquid as the closest to strengthening that connection. Trade.XYZ, which operates most of the platform’s traditional-market contracts, reportedly splits trading fees equally with Hyperliquid, whose share largely supports HYPE buybacks.

There is a catch: Trade.XYZ is operating with trading fees discounted by more than 90% to attract users. The YouTube video says those discounts are expected to shrink as markets mature, potentially increasing buyback funding, although higher fees could also change trading behavior.

ONDO presents a different problem. Fire Hustle says Ondo Finance surpassed $4 billion in total value locked, including more than $1.3 billion in tokenized stocks and ETFs, while ONDO holders currently receive no direct fee distributions, buybacks or burns.

A holder-led forum proposal would direct 20% of revenue toward token buybacks and burns, eventually rising to 40%. The host stresses that it is not an approved policy and says the team had not responded.

Crucially, the $4 billion figure represents assets deposited, not revenue available to distribute.

Injective already links application revenue to INJ buybacks and burns, according to the video. But its scale remains modest: the host cites roughly $215 million in traditional-market trading over 30 days and a largest buyback round of about $315,000.

The potential catalyst is Pineapple Prime, a planned mortgage-yield product.

More than $1 billion in mortgage records reportedly moved onto Injective, but the host makes an important distinction: those records are data, not yet money flowing through a live investment product.

In conclusion, these are three way different bets: higher fee capture, an unapproved governance change and a product launch.

None makes trading growth equivalent to token returns, especially when discounted fees, limited activity and concentrated infrastructure can interrupt the connection.

#5178. Senate Hearing Could Shape the SEC’s Next Chapter for Crypto Oversight

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The US Senate Banking Committee is preparing to examine nominees for positions at the Securities and Exchange Commission, a development that could eventually influence the tone and priorities of crypto oversight. A hearing scheduled for Thursday, November 19, puts personnel decisions back in the spotlight at a time when industry participants are seeking clearer rules on token offerings, custody and trading venues.

Hearings are part of the appointment process, not the end of it. An appearance before senators does not amount to confirmation, and nominees' eventual influence will depend on their responsibilities, the agency's composition and the laws it must enforce.

CoinDesk reported that the Banking Committee had scheduled a November 19 hearing involving SEC nominees Steven Levine and Kristin Johnson. The proceedings are expected to give senators an opportunity to question the candidates on their approach to securities regulation, though what they actually say should be judged from the hearing record rather than predicted in advance.

The same reporting discussed separate nominees for roles at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The CFTC's appointment process is not identical to the SEC's, and a hearing for one agency should not be read as an automatic timetable for the other. Both agencies affect digital-asset activity, but their legal jurisdictions and responsibilities differ.

Businesses building token markets often want to know which rules apply before launching a product, not after it has attracted users. Questions can include whether an asset or particular transaction falls within securities law, how intermediaries should register and what disclosures are expected. Regulatory staff and commissioners shape policy through rulemaking, enforcement decisions and public guidance, although courts and Congress also have important roles.

A change in personnel can influence priorities, but it does not instantly rewrite the rules. Existing statutes remain in force, earlier litigation can continue and new policy proposals may need formal procedures. For a company considering a US product launch, a nomination is therefore a signal to monitor rather than a substitute for legal advice or an enacted regulation.

Prediction markets and derivative instruments illustrate the difficulty of drawing clear regulatory lines. NewsBTC's earlier coverage of litigation involving Coinbase, Kalshi and the CFTC demonstrates how novel products can trigger disputes over oversight and market structure. The SEC and CFTC do not necessarily reach the same questions through the same legal framework.

International developments also provide a reminder that the United States does not set standards in isolation. European tokenisation discussions covered by NewsBTC show regulators elsewhere trying to align traditional financial protections with new technology. US appointees will face the task of balancing market integrity, investor protection and innovation against a global competitive backdrop.

Specific answers about custody, market intermediaries, token distributions and enforcement philosophy would be more informative than general pledges to support innovation or protect consumers. Written responses and subsequent votes are worth watching too. Yet even a persuasive performance at a hearing offers no guarantee of confirmation or a particular policy outcome.

The near-term event is clear: November 19 provides a public checkpoint for the SEC nominees. What follows may shape the regulatory conversation over months and years. Treating a personnel hearing as an immediate market catalyst would be a much bigger claim than the available evidence supports.

#5177. Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B in Physical Gold Backing

Tether's gold-backed stablecoin, Tether Gold (XAUT), has completed its first full audit by KPMG, which found the token fully backed by physical gold, the company announced on Thursday.

KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements of TG Commodities, which issues XAUT, for the year ended December 31, 2025. An unqualified, or "clean," opinion means the auditor found that the statements fairly present the company's financial position, without reservations.

Tether Gold (XAU₮) Becomes Tether’s Second Stablecoin to Complete a Big Four AuditLearn more: https://t.co/eO0asUwvlI

As of the end of 2025, TG Commodities held 520,089.350 troy ounces of allocated gold, valued at $2.246 billion, against 520,089.300 XAUT tokens in issue, according to Tether. The gold is held in vaults in Switzerland, and each token represents an ownership interest in gold on specific bars.

As part of the audit, KPMG physically counted and inspected every gold bar backing the token, rather than relying only on confirmations from custodians, Tether said.

"KPMG counted every single bar as part of its Tether Gold audit," Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said, adding that he believes XAUT "is on track to become the first true competitor to the gold ETF market."

The XAUT audit is Tether's second by a Big Four firm. In August, KPMG issued a clean opinion on Tether International, the issuer of its flagship USDT stablecoin, in what the company called the largest inaugural audit in history, Decrypt reported at the time.

For years, Tether faced criticism for relying on quarterly attestations, which offer a snapshot of reserves at a single point in time, rather than a full audit of its finances. The company first said earlier this year that it was being audited by a Big Four firm without naming it, before confirming KPMG.

Tether still publishes quarterly attestations for USDT. Its latest, prepared by accounting firm BDO and covering the period to September 30, showed total reserve assets of $191.5 billion against $183.5 billion in liabilities, giving it an excess reserve buffer of almost $8 billion, according to the report. Tether said it made $1.5 billion in net operating profit in the third quarter.

"These milestones advance the progress towards audits across the whole of Tether," said chief financial officer Simon McWilliams.

Separately from the gold backing XAUT, Tether has also built up its own large gold reserves, and Ardoino has said it will keep adding to its stash, which it stores in a former nuclear bunker in Switzerland.

#5176. Meta’s Internal Prediction App Uses Points, Not Cash — and That Distinction Matters

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Meta is reportedly experimenting with a prediction game for employees in which participants forecast outcomes using points rather than real money. That may sound like a small internal product test, but it offers an interesting window into how large technology companies are thinking about forecasting, social engagement and the mechanics behind prediction markets.

The essential distinction is that a points-based game is not automatically a cash-settled financial market. No public launch or real-money service has been confirmed in the reporting on the experiment, so it would be misleading to describe Meta as having entered the regulated betting or event-contract business.

The Block, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Meta was testing an employee application known as Takes, previously called Arena. Participants can make forecasts and earn or lose an internal points balance referred to as cred. The structure resembles a prediction market in some respects, but without the same money flows or legal arrangements as a traded contract.

An internal trial can help answer useful product questions. Do people enjoy making forecasts? How should results be scored? Does a ranking system reward genuine insight or simply encourage attention-grabbing guesses? Those questions matter whether the eventual outcome is a staff game, a public social feature or nothing at all. The existence of a test does not establish which direction Meta will choose.

Real-money prediction markets can involve financial risk, market manipulation concerns, customer eligibility, settlement disputes and questions about gambling or derivatives law. A points-based contest may avoid some of those features, depending on its design. But a game can still have integrity problems if employees feel encouraged to trade on private information or if forecasts become workplace performance signals.

There is also a difference between a prediction with a numerical score and a security or derivative. Those categories are shaped by contract terms and applicable law, not simply by whether the interface looks like a market. Readers should be cautious when comparing an internal staff experiment directly with companies offering event contracts to paying customers.

Regulated prediction markets are attracting scrutiny from federal and state authorities, particularly around sports-related contracts. NewsBTC previously examined a CFTC-related lawsuit involving Coinbase and Kalshi, an example of how disputes over jurisdiction can arise as firms offer products that do not fit neatly into traditional categories.

That uncertainty makes Meta's use of non-cash points noteworthy. A platform can learn about user participation and forecasting behaviour without immediately building the custody, settlement and compliance systems required for real-money products. Whether that is the strategic reason for the design has not been established; it is simply a material distinction between the two models.

Big companies routinely trial features that never reach the public. Employee feedback can reveal problems early, and an internal rename does not by itself mean a product is ready for commercial deployment. Similarly, parallels with AI-agent payment experiments covered by NewsBTC show how companies use small tests to explore unfamiliar transaction designs before the market is settled.

The next meaningful development would be an official description of the experiment's objectives, product scope or possible external release. Until then, Takes is best understood as a reported internal forecasting test — an interesting sign of curiosity, but not evidence that Meta has launched a new exchange.

The firm now holds 14.17 million AVAX, with 99.7% of this amount staked at an annualized rate of 5.85%. Moreover, the treasury repurchased 384K shares in Q3 and another 701K shares in October.

Altogether, the altcoin is now seeing exposure to institutional capital and growing DeFi activity. This could strengthen the network’s momentum, even though the price charts aren’t exactly looking pretty.

At the time of writing, AVAX was testing a key support level as its price extended the sideways range between $8 and $9. Despite the scale of participation and buying activity from AVAX One, these efforts aren’t exactly translating into real demand.

The level could break and test $7.82 as selling momentum gains pace. The resurgence of the red MACD histogram seemed to hint the same too.

From the market structure, the altcoin may rebound from the $8-level as it has done over the past five instances.

On the other hand, bears may break down the level as the broader market is weak. That puts $7 as the next demand level where bulls could return.

#5174. Crypto Traders Blame Binance for Bitcoin Drop, But Data Points to Coinbase

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. According to CoinGlass, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on the Coinbase spot market reached -$1.08 billion between Oct. 31 and Nov. 15. CVD shows the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

The price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

The data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some users on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that showed client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several users in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

Coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

Anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

The CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.

#5173. XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

XRP exchange balances have reached a one-year high, while the share of tokens untouched for over a year nears its annual peak.

XRP held on exchanges has reached a one-year high even as the share of coins untouched for more than a year approaches its own annual peak, according to figures cited by wealth-focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson.

Her latest video examines that split following a roughly 10% price decline, arguing that investors’ financial circumstances can matter as much as their market convictions.

Stevenson cites CryptoQuant data showing approximately 11.8 billion XRP on exchanges, the highest balance in a year. That puts more tokens within easy reach of trading, although exchange deposits alone do not establish that holders intend to sell.

Meanwhile, Glassnode figures cited in the video put the share of XRP unmoved for more than a year at roughly 56%, up from 51% in January. Stevenson also says XRP exchange-traded funds still hold about 1.19 billion tokens, despite a small outflow ending a reported 13-week inflow streak.

“Both groups saw the same price,” she says. “They reacted to it in completely opposite ways.”

The contrast is striking, but the metrics have limits. Coins remaining stationary demonstrate inactivity, not necessarily fresh buying or confidence, and neither measure establishes where XRP’s price goes next.

Dr. Stevenson identifies three recurring sources of selling pressure: leverage, investing money needed for near-term expenses, and entering a volatile market without a plan.

She cites roughly $25.7 million in XRP liquidations on Binance during a recent sell-off as an example of positions being closed regardless of investors’ intentions.

Her broader bullish case rests partly on institutional activity involving Ripple and its RLUSD stablecoin.

The YouTube video names Standard Chartered, Cross River Bank and DriveWealth among firms involved in custody, banking or settlement developments.

Those developments should not be treated as equivalent to demand for XRP itself. Nor does institutional infrastructure guarantee that token prices will recover.

The most durable point is about liquidity: cash reserves and manageable exposure reduce the likelihood that an unexpected bill or margin call dictates a sale.

Exchange balances may signal potential selling pressure across the market; they cannot reveal which holders can afford to wait.

#5172. Louisiana and CFTC Clash Over Who Regulates Prediction Markets

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A confrontation between Louisiana officials and the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is sharpening the dispute over who gets to regulate prediction markets. The state has pursued restrictions on certain event-contract offerings, while the federal agency has gone to court asserting its authority. The dispute could affect platforms offering sports and other outcome-based contracts, but the legal arguments have not yet produced a final nationwide answer.

It is a case where the exact stage of litigation matters. Temporary orders, complaints and jurisdictional claims are not final findings about which side is right.

The Block reported that a Louisiana state court issued a temporary restraining order on November 12 involving a group of prediction-market and related businesses. The state's approach seeks to require geographic restrictions for certain offerings that it says should not be available without appropriate state authorisation. Firms named in the proceedings reportedly include Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase and Robinhood among a wider set.

An order of this kind is designed to address immediate concerns while further litigation continues. Its existence does not establish that every product mentioned is unlawful under all circumstances. Different platforms may offer different types of contracts, and the precise language of the order and subsequent court rulings determines what each respondent must do.

The CFTC filed a federal complaint on November 13 as the dispute escalated. Federal commodities law gives the agency important powers over derivatives markets, but state authorities have their own responsibilities for gambling and consumer protection. The central legal question is where one set of powers ends and the other begins when an event contract resembles both a derivative and a bet on an outcome.

The disagreement is not merely political theatre. Companies need clear boundaries to decide which products may be offered, how users must be screened and what licences or approvals are necessary. Conflicting instructions from different levels of government can be expensive to implement and difficult for customers to understand.

For an operator, an adverse ruling might mean geofencing customers, suspending products or changing contract design. For users, it might affect whether an existing market remains accessible in their location and what protections apply if a dispute arises. These potential consequences make the litigation commercially significant even before the courts resolve the larger federalism question.

NewsBTC's earlier account of CFTC-related litigation involving Coinbase and Kalshi offers useful background on the expanding legal debate around event and derivative markets. A single case, however, should not be treated as decisive precedent for every possible contract category.

Reporting identifies November 30 as a date to watch in the Louisiana proceedings. Whether temporary restrictions remain in force, are modified or expire can depend on procedural developments before then. Readers should also monitor the federal case independently, as it may follow a different timetable and raise distinct legal questions.

Other jurisdictions are wrestling with how to supervise new financial infrastructure, including tokenisation standards in Europe. Louisiana's dispute is a particularly sharp example of the same underlying problem: innovation does not arrive organised according to existing regulator boundaries. Until courts and lawmakers clarify those boundaries, platforms will continue to operate amid uncertainty rather than a settled national rulebook.

XRP’s institutional demand has been growing at an accelerating rate. The first U.S XRP ETF was launched a year ago and since then, they have accumulated about 1.16 billion tokens.

This amount is equivalent to $1.15 billion, representing around 1.77% of XRP’s market cap. However, the cumulative total net inflows were worth $1.79 billion at press time.

This disparity in total net assets held and cumulative net inflows comes from the decline in price over the past few weeks.

The major institutions taking the lead on XRP’s accumulation are Bitwise, Franklin Templeton, Canary Capital, 21Shares, Grayscale, and REX-Osprey.

This hinted at institutional exposure, even though $1.09 million in capital left as the markets closed for the weekend. Even so, the overall outlook seemed to indicate that the circulating supply of the altcoin is being absorbed at a bigger scale.

While institutions were buying XRP, the altcoin was crashing on the charts due to massive selling. Despite a 40% decline to $0.99 and losing the $1-psychological level, U.S investors seem to be returning.

The net buying trend of XRP on Coinbase turned positive over the past two consecutive days. The hourly charts showed that more than 4 million XRP were longed by U.S investors after a period of heavy selling.

However, the metric stayed negative on Binance and OKX exchanges, though it was trading near the neutral level. In fact, the figures on OKX and Binance spiked above the neutral level before retracing shortly after.

This was a signal that traders’ activity was slowly shifting with the dip below $1.

At the same time, indicators were starting to show signs that the 40% correction from $1.66 to $0.99 was about to end. The TD Sequential printed a buy signal on the daily charts after two months of decline.

The daily trading volume showed that about 2.09 million tokens were bought at press time. The Stochastic RSI also bounced from oversold territory to 41.64, hinting at the return of buying pressure on smaller timeframes.

However, the altcoin still remains well below the 200-day SMA at $1.26, indicating that the bigger trend may bebear-controlled. If $1 could be reclaimed, a recovery towards $1.15 and $1.26 could follow.

Conversely, losing the $0.98-$0.99-level could expose $0.80 or lower levels. The ongoing correction is likely to continue unless a clear market structure flip happens.
